scheme_details.tagline: Direct income support of ₹6,000 per year to all landholding farmer families.
scheme_details.department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.overview: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) is a Central Sector Scheme that provides income support to all landholding farmers' families across the country to enable them to take care of expenses related to agriculture and allied activities as well as domestic needs.
eligibility: All landholding farmer families possessing cultivable land in their names.
Subject to exclusion categories (e.g., institutional landholders, active/retired government employees, professionals like doctors/engineers, income tax payers, and high-income pensioners).

money_benefits.direct_financial_support: ₹6,000 per year in three equal installments of ₹2,000 directly into the bank accounts of farmers.

benefits: Financial assistance of ₹6,000 annually.
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) prevents leakages.
Helps farmers purchase seeds, fertilizers, and cover farming expenses.
Reduces dependency on informal money lenders.
documents_required: Land Ownership Documents / Land Revenue Records (Khasra/Khatauni)
application_process: Visit the official PM-KISAN portal (pmkisan.gov.in) and navigate to the 'Farmers Corner'.
Click on 'New Farmer Registration' and enter your Aadhaar Number and Mobile Number.
Fill out the state, district, sub-district, block, and village details.
Enter personal details, bank account details, and land parcel details (survey number, dag number, area).
Upload land documents and click submit.
The application is sent to State Nodal Officers for verification.
Upon validation, the benefits are credited in the next installment cycle.
scheme_details.important_dates: Ongoing enrollment. Installments are released thrice a year: April-July, August-November, and December-March.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for PM-KISAN?
faqs.answer: All landholding farmer families with cultivable land in their names are eligible, except those falling under exclusion criteria (like income tax payers, government employees, or institutional landholders).

faqs.question: Is eKYC mandatory for PM-KISAN?
faqs.answer: Yes, eKYC is mandatory for all registered farmers to receive further installments.

faqs.question: How do I check my payment status?
faqs.answer: You can check your status on the official website under 'Know Your Status' by entering your Registration Number or mobile number.

scheme_details.tagline: Hassle-free access to short-term credit for crop cultivation and agricultural maintenance.
scheme_details.department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.implemented_by: Commercial Banks, Cooperative Banks, and Regional Rural Banks (RRBs)
scheme_details.overview: The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme provides farmers with timely access to credit for crop production, post-harvest expenses, marketing loans, consumption requirements, and working capital for allied activities (fisheries, animal husbandry) at highly subsidized interest rates.
eligibility: Owner cultivators (individual or joint).
Tenant farmers, oral lessees, and sharecroppers.
Self-Help Groups (SHGs) or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) of farmers.
Farmers engaged in animal husbandry, poultry, and fisheries.
scheme_details.land_limit: Applicant must possess or cultivate agricultural land. No minimum or maximum land holding specified.

money_benefits.interest_subvention: Short-term crop loans up to ₹3 lakh at 7% per annum interest, reduced to 4% per annum upon prompt repayment (3% prompt repayment incentive).
money_benefits.credit_limit: Determined based on cropping pattern, scale of finance, and land holding size.

benefits: Flexible credit withdrawal limit to buy seeds, fertilizers, and rent equipment.
Subsidized interest rate as low as 4% per annum.
Includes accidental insurance coverage (up to ₹50,000 for disability/death).
No collateral required for loans up to ₹1.6 lakh (extended to ₹3 lakh in some cases).
documents_required: Aadhaar Card / Voter ID Card / PAN Card
Land Holding Certificate (Pattadar Passbook / Land tax receipts)
Details of crops sown or cropping pattern
application_process: Visit the bank branch where you have a savings account or apply online via the bank's net banking portal.
Fill out the Kisan Credit Card application form with crop and land details.
Attach identity proof, address proof, and land ownership records.
Submit the application to the loan officer.
The bank will conduct land verification and assess your creditworthiness.
Once approved, the bank sanctions the loan limit and issues a RuPay Kisan Credit Card.
scheme_details.important_dates: Applications are accepted throughout the year. Credit limits are renewed annually.

faqs.question: What is the interest rate for KCC loans?
faqs.answer: The nominal interest rate is 7% per annum. However, if you repay the loan on time, the government provides a 3% interest subvention, making the effective interest rate only 4%.

faqs.question: Can tenant farmers apply for KCC?
faqs.answer: Yes, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, and oral lessees are eligible to apply.

faqs.question: What is the limit for collateral-free loans under KCC?
faqs.answer: KCC loans up to ₹1.6 lakh do not require any collateral or security.

scheme_details.tagline: Old age pension scheme providing social security to small and marginal farmers.
scheme_details.department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.implemented_by: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) and Common Service Centres (CSC)
scheme_details.overview: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana is a voluntary and contributory pension scheme for small and marginal farmers to secure their livelihoods in old age. On attaining 60 years of age, eligible beneficiaries receive a monthly pension of ₹3,000.
eligibility: Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs) who own cultivable land up to 2 hectares.
Must be an Indian citizen.
Age between 18 and 40 years.
Should not be covered under other social security schemes (like NPS, EPFO, ESIC) or be an income tax payer.

money_benefits.matching_contribution: Government contributes an equal amount to the pension fund as paid by the farmer (ranging from ₹55 to ₹200 per month based on entry age).

benefits: Guaranteed monthly pension of ₹3,000 upon reaching 60 years.
Spouse family pension of 50% (₹1,500/month) if the beneficiary passes away.
Voluntary exit options with interest if the farmer chooses to leave the scheme early.
documents_required: Consent form for auto-debit of monthly contributions
application_process: Visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or register online through maandhan.in.
Provide your Aadhaar number, date of birth, bank details, and land records to the operator.
The system calculates the monthly premium based on your age (e.g., ₹55 at age 18, up to ₹200 at age 40).
Sign the auto-debit mandate form so contributions are automatically deducted from your bank account.
The enrollment agent submits the data and generates a Kisan Pension Card containing your Unique Pension Account Number (KPAN).
scheme_details.important_dates: Ongoing enrollment. Farmers must contribute monthly until they reach 60 years of age.

faqs.question: What happens if the beneficiary dies before age 60?
faqs.answer: If the farmer dies before age 60, their spouse has the option to continue the contributions or exit the scheme and receive the accumulated corpus with interest.

faqs.question: How much does a farmer need to contribute?
faqs.answer: The monthly contribution ranges from ₹55 (for age 18) to ₹200 (for age 40). The government contributes an equal matching amount.

scheme_details.tagline: Financial security against crop loss due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases.
scheme_details.department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.overview: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is a crop insurance scheme designed to support sustainable agriculture by providing financial protection to farmers suffering from crop damage or yield losses caused by weather anomalies, pests, or plant diseases.
eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers.
The scheme is voluntary for all farmers (loanee and non-loanee alike).

money_benefits.premium_subsidy: Farmers pay a nominal premium: 2% of sum insured for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for commercial/horticultural crops. The rest of the premium is heavily subsidized by the government.
money_benefits.claim_payout: Direct credit to the farmer's bank account based on estimated yield loss compared to historical average.

benefits: Comprehensive risk insurance covering prevented sowing, mid-season adversity, standing crop losses, and post-harvest losses.
Extremely low premiums for farmers.
Fast, automated claim settlements based on crop cutting experiments (CCE) and satellite imagery.
application_process: Register online on the PMFBY portal (pmfby.gov.in) or visit your nearest bank branch, cooperative society, or Common Service Centre (CSC).
Provide details of sown crops, land survey numbers, and bank accounts.
Pay the applicable farmer premium amount (1.5%, 2%, or 5% of sum insured).
Receive an acknowledgment receipt with an application number.
In case of localized crop loss (hailstorm, inundation, landslide), report the damage within 72 hours via the Crop Insurance App or to the local agriculture department.
scheme_details.important_dates: Separate deadlines for Kharif (typically July 31) and Rabi (typically December 31) enrollment.

faqs.question: What crops are covered under PMFBY?
faqs.answer: Food crops (cereals, millets, pulses), oilseeds, and annual commercial/horticultural crops notified by the state government.

faqs.question: Is PMFBY mandatory for loanee farmers?
faqs.answer: No, PMFBY is fully voluntary. Loanee farmers can opt-out by submitting a written request to their bank before the enrollment deadline.

faqs.question: How do I report crop damage?
faqs.answer: Crop damage must be reported within 72 hours of the occurrence through the 'Crop Insurance' mobile app, nearest bank branch, or the local agriculture officer.

scheme_details.tagline: National mission for financial inclusion ensuring access to banking and insurance services.
scheme_details.department: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
scheme_details.implemented_by: Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, and Regional Rural Banks
scheme_details.overview: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is a national mission on financial inclusion to ensure access to financial services, namely, basic savings bank accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, and pensions for unbanked households, especially in rural areas.
eligibility: Any Indian citizen who does not have an existing bank account.
Minors above the age of 10 can open a basic savings account under guardianship.

money_benefits.overdraft_facility: Overdraft facility up to ₹10,000 available to eligible account holders after 6 months of satisfactory transaction history.
money_benefits.accidental_insurance: Free accidental insurance cover of ₹2,000,000 for accounts opened after August 2018 (with RuPay debit cards).
money_benefits.life_insurance: Life insurance cover of ₹30,000 (subject to criteria).

benefits: Zero balance savings account (no minimum balance required).
Interest is earned on deposits.
Issue of RuPay Debit Card for easy withdrawals and digital transactions.
Enables seamless direct benefit transfer (DBT) of government subsidies directly into the account.
documents_required: Aadhaar Card (If Aadhaar has address, it serves as ID & Address proof)
Alternatively: Voter ID, PAN Card, Driving License, Passport, or NREGA Job Card
application_process: Visit the nearest bank branch, customer service point (CSP), or Bank Mitra.
Obtain the PMJDY account opening form.
Fill out the form, specifying personal details, nominee details, and contact information.
Submit self-attested copies of Aadhaar or other officially valid documents.
The bank mitras verify the details and activate the zero-balance account.
Receive your RuPay debit card and welcome kit.
scheme_details.important_dates: Ongoing enrollment. Accounts can be opened on any banking day.

faqs.question: Can I open an account with zero balance under PMJDY?
faqs.answer: Yes, PMJDY accounts are Basic Savings Bank Deposit Accounts (BSBDA) which can be opened and operated with zero balance.

faqs.question: What is the overdraft limit?
faqs.answer: Eligible account holders can get an overdraft of up to ₹10,000. Up to ₹2,000 can be availed without any conditions.

scheme_details.tagline: Promoting climate-resilient farming, water conservation, and soil health management.
scheme_details.department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.implemented_by: State Departments of Agriculture and Soil Conservation Nodal Agencies
scheme_details.overview: National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) aims to make agriculture more productive, sustainable, and climate-resilient by promoting water-use efficiency, conservation of natural resources, integrated farming systems, soil health management, and sustainable rainfed technologies.
eligibility: Individual farmers, farmer groups, cooperatives, and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs).
Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups.
Priority is given to farmers in rainfed, drought-prone, and climate-vulnerable zones.

money_benefits.farming_subsidy: Financial assistance ranging from 40% to 50% for setting up integrated farming systems, purchasing micro-irrigation equipment, constructing farm ponds, and adopting organic farming inputs.
money_benefits.soil_testing: Free or highly subsidized soil testing services and provision of Soil Health Cards.

benefits: Increases crop productivity in rainfed areas through water harvesting and conservation.
Promotes organic farming, reducing chemical costs.
Ensures balanced fertilizer application using Soil Health Cards.
Supports crop diversification and agroforestry to boost income resilience.
application_process: Visit your district's Agriculture Department office or Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK).
Obtain the NMSA application form specific to the component (e.g., Rainfed Area Development, Soil Health Management).
Fill in land details, cropping history, and choose the sustainable farming model.
Attach land records, bank details, and submit the form.
Agriculture officers will inspect the land site to verify eligibility.
Subsidies are disbursed directly via DBT after implementation of activities.
scheme_details.important_dates: Schemes are implemented annually in accordance with state agricultural action plans.

faqs.question: What is a Soil Health Card?
faqs.answer: A printed report given to a farmer containing the status of his soil in terms of 12 nutrients, with recommended dosage of fertilizers to improve yield.

faqs.question: What is Rainfed Area Development (RAD)?
faqs.answer: A component under NMSA that promotes integrated farming systems (combining crops, horticulture, livestock, fishery) to ensure multi-source income in dry areas.

scheme_details.tagline: Financing post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.
scheme_details.department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.implemented_by: Scheduled Commercial Banks, Cooperative Banks, RRBs, and National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC)
scheme_details.overview: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) is a medium-to-long term debt financing facility for investment in viable projects for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets through interest subvention and financial support.
eligibility: Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Marketing Cooperative Societies, and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs).
Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), and Multipurpose Cooperative Societies.
Agri-entrepreneurs, startups, and individual farmers.

money_benefits.interest_subvention: Interest subvention of 3% per annum on loans up to ₹2 crore for a maximum period of 7 years.
money_benefits.credit_guarantee: Credit guarantee coverage under CGTMSE scheme for loans up to ₹2 crore without collateral.

benefits: Allows setting up cold storage, packhouses, silos, sorting/grading units, and ripening chambers.
Reduces post-harvest losses and enables farmers to store crops for better prices.
Lower interest rate on agri-infrastructure loans.
Promotes agricultural entrepreneurship and startups.
documents_required: Detailed Project Report (DPR) of the proposed infrastructure
Aadhaar Card and PAN Card of the applicant
Land ownership documents or lease agreement for the project site
Bank statement and financial records of the entity
application_process: Go to the official AIF portal (agriinfra.dac.gov.in).
Click on 'Beneficiary Registration' and fill in mobile and Aadhaar details.
Upload your Detailed Project Report (DPR) detailing project cost, feasibility, and bank preference.
The application is screened by the Project Management Unit (PMU) for eligibility.
Once approved, the application is forwarded online to the selected lending bank.
The bank conducts due diligence, sanctions the loan with 3% interest subvention, and disburses the amount.
scheme_details.important_dates: The scheme is active for funding projects until 2025-26, with interest subventions extending up to 2032-33.

faqs.question: What projects can be financed under AIF?
faqs.answer: Projects like warehouses, cold chains, primary processing centers, sorting/grading units, custom hiring centers, and organic input manufacturing units.

faqs.question: What is the maximum loan limit under AIF?
faqs.answer: There is no cap on the loan amount, but the 3% interest subvention is restricted to a maximum loan amount of ₹2 crore per project.

scheme_details.tagline: Pension security for citizens in the unorganized sector, including agricultural workers.
scheme_details.department: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
scheme_details.implemented_by: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) via Banks and Post Offices
scheme_details.overview: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is a government-backed pension scheme aimed at creating a universal social security system, particularly targeting workers in the unorganized sector (like farm laborers, artisans, small traders) to provide them with a stable income source after retirement.
eligibility: Must be an Indian citizen.
Age between 18 and 40 years.
Must have a savings bank account linked to Aadhaar and mobile.
Must not be an income tax payer and should not be covered under statutory social security schemes.

money_benefits.guaranteed_pension: Minimum guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000, ₹2,000, ₹3,000, ₹4,000, or ₹5,000 starting at age 60.
money_benefits.death_benefit: In case of subscriber's death, the pension goes to the spouse. If both die, the accumulated pension corpus is returned to the nominee.

benefits: Fixed retirement income starting at 60.
Low-risk and government-guaranteed retirement plan.
Auto-debit facility removes the hassle of manual payments.
application_process: Visit your bank branch or post office where you maintain a savings account.
Fill out the APY registration form, detailing personal info, pension slab choice, and nominee info.
Provide authorization for auto-debit of monthly/quarterly contributions.
Ensure your bank account has sufficient balance on the debit dates to avoid late payment penalties.
A PRAN (Permanent Retirement Account Number) card will be generated and sent to you.
scheme_details.important_dates: Ongoing enrollment. Contributions must be paid regularly until age 60.

faqs.question: Can I increase or decrease my pension amount later?
faqs.answer: Yes, subscribers can scale up or scale down their pension configurations once a year during the month of July.

faqs.question: Are income-tax payers eligible for APY?
faqs.answer: No, with effect from October 1, 2022, citizens who are or have been income-tax payers are not eligible to join APY.

scheme_details.tagline: A 14-digit unique alpha-numeric identifier (Bhu-Aadhaar) for every land parcel in India.
scheme_details.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development
scheme_details.implemented_by: State Revenue Departments and National Informatics Centre (NIC)
scheme_details.overview: Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN), also called Bhu-Aadhaar, is a scheme to assign a unique 14-digit alpha-numeric identity number to every survey land parcel in India. It is generated using the latitude-longitude coordinates of the land parcel.
eligibility: All registered land owners and farmers in states where ULPIN is implemented.
scheme_details.land_limit: Applicable to all registered land parcels
benefits: Acts as a single, authentic source of land information.
Prevents land fraud, double sales, and boundary disputes.
Facilitates easy credit/loans from banks by verifying land ownership instantly.
Enables seamless transaction and mutation tracking.
documents_required: Land ownership records / RoR (Record of Rights)
application_process: No direct applicant registration is required. State revenue departments conduct geo-referencing of land plots using GIS.
Once boundary maps are digitized, a 14-digit ULPIN is automatically generated for the land parcel.
Land owners can view their ULPIN (Bhu-Aadhaar) on their state's digital land records portal (e.g., Bhulekh) by entering their district, village, and survey/khasra numbers.
scheme_details.important_dates: Ongoing rollout across all states under the Digital India Land Records program.

faqs.question: How is ULPIN calculated?
faqs.answer: ULPIN is generated based on the geo-coordinates (longitude and latitude) of the polygon vertices of the land parcel.

faqs.question: How do farmers benefit from Bhu-Aadhaar?
faqs.answer: It serves as clear proof of land ownership, making it extremely easy to apply for crop insurance, receive direct benefit transfers, and get collateral-free bank loans.

title: Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme

scheme_details.tagline: Modernizing land administration and digitization of land records and maps.
scheme_details.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development
scheme_details.overview: The Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) is a major reform to digitize land records, spatial maps (cadastral maps), survey registries, and to computerize registration processes, moving towards a transparent and guaranteed land titling system.
eligibility: All land owners, farmers, and agricultural workers in India.
benefits: Access to land records online anytime, eliminating physical visits to revenue offices.
Tamper-proof land records reduce corruption and litigation.
Speeds up the land mutation process (transfer of ownership) upon sale or inheritance.
Enables single-window service for maps, registration, and land records.
application_process: Visit your state's official Land Records Portal (e.g., Bhulekh, Dharani, AnyROR).
Search for your land using Survey Number, Khata Number, or Owner Name.
You can print a digitally signed copy of the Record of Rights (RoR/Bhulekh) online.
For property registration, book an online slot, visit the sub-registrar office, and get deeds digitized instantly.
scheme_details.important_dates: Continuous program implemented in phases across all states.

faqs.question: Can I check my land records online?
faqs.answer: Yes, most states have digitized land records accessible through their official web portals (such as Bhulekh) where you can download copies of land maps and RoR.

faqs.question: What is land mutation?
faqs.answer: Land mutation is the process of transferring the ownership name in the local revenue records from the seller to the buyer after a sale or inheritance.

title: Indian Council of Agricultural Research Services

scheme_details.tagline: Linking agricultural research, education, and extension services for farming communities.
scheme_details.department: Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.implemented_by: ICAR Institutes, Agricultural Universities, and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs)
scheme_details.overview: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is the apex national body coordinating, guiding, and managing research and education in agriculture including horticulture, fisheries, and animal sciences. Through KVKs, it provides training and tech solutions directly to farmers.
eligibility: All active farmers, crop growers, organic producers, agri-researchers, and students in India.
benefits: Free access to high-yielding seed varieties developed by ICAR.
Free training programs on modern crop management, livestock rearing, and food processing.
On-farm demonstrations and expert advice from KVK scientists.
Access to weather forecasts, pest alerts, and mobile advisories.
documents_required: Farmer registration under local KVK portal
application_process: Visit your nearest district Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or the official ICAR portal (icar.org.in).
Enroll in the Kisan Mobile Advisory Services (KMAS) to receive agricultural advisory SMS.
Register for short-term training programs on crop cultivation, organic farming, beekeeping, dairy, or poultry.
Purchase high-quality seed varieties and bio-fertilizers directly from the KVK sales counter.
scheme_details.important_dates: Training schedules and advisory programs are organized throughout the year depending on sowing seasons.

faqs.question: What is a Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK)?
faqs.answer: A KVK is an agricultural science centre established in every district by ICAR to act as a bridge between lab research and field application for farmers.

faqs.question: How can I contact ICAR scientists for crop problems?
faqs.answer: Farmers can visit their local KVK, call the toll-free national farmer helpline, or use the ICAR Krishi mobile app to upload photos of pests/diseases and get recommendations.

scheme_details.tagline: Abolition of intermediaries, tenancy reforms, and distribution of surplus land to landless.
scheme_details.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development
scheme_details.implemented_by: State Revenue and Land Reform Departments
scheme_details.overview: The Land Reforms Programme is a historic and ongoing state-led initiative to bring structural changes in land ownership. It focuses on the abolition of Zamindari systems, securing tenancy rights, implementing ceiling limits on land holdings, and distributing ceiling-surplus land to the landless poor.
eligibility: Landless agricultural laborers, small and marginal farmers, and rural families belonging to disadvantaged sections (SC/ST).
benefits: Empowers landless laborers by granting them ownership of cultivable plots.
Protects tenants from arbitrary eviction and guarantees fair rents.
Ensures equitable distribution of land resources in rural communities.
documents_required: BPL (Below Poverty Line) card / Income proof
application_process: Eligible candidates can apply for ceiling-surplus land allotment during distribution drives conducted by local block/tehsil revenue officers.
Submit proof of landless status, income, and category details.
Revenue departments verify the application and conduct local inquiries.
Once approved, land titles (Patta) are distributed to beneficiaries, and records are mutated.
scheme_details.important_dates: Varies state-by-state, typically coordinated during specific land-allotment campaigns.

faqs.question: What is Zamindari abolition?
faqs.answer: It is the removal of the old intermediary landlord system, giving direct land titles to the actual cultivators who were previously tenant farmers.

faqs.question: What is land ceiling?
faqs.answer: A legal limit on the maximum amount of land an individual or family can own. Land exceeding this limit is declared surplus and distributed to landless poor.

scheme_details.tagline: Revitalizing drylands and rainfed regions through watershed management.
scheme_details.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development
scheme_details.implemented_by: State Watershed Nodal Agencies in partnership with the World Bank
scheme_details.overview: The Neeranchal National Watershed Project is designed to strengthen the Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) by improving water harvesting, soil moisture retention, land restoration, and sustainable agricultural practices in drylands and rainfed farming systems.
eligibility: Communities and farmers residing in notified watershed development regions, rainfed zones, and drought-prone districts.

money_benefits.watershed_grant: Funding support provided to local Watershed Committees for water conservation structures, check dams, and agroforestry models.

benefits: Recharges groundwater tables, increasing water availability for irrigation.
Controls soil erosion and improves crop yields in dry areas.
Supports secondary livelihoods like horticulture, dairy, and fisheries in rural regions.
Helps farmers mitigate dry spells and climate risks.
documents_required: Land ownership records (within the watershed boundary)
Certificate of residence in the watershed village
application_process: Neeranchal operates as a community-led development program.
Watershed planning and structures are decided by the Village Watershed Committee (WCC) during Gram Sabhas.
Farmers submit land boundary details to participate in bunding, farm pond excavation, or dryland farming training.
The project funds are directly used to build community water structures and provide subsidized seed/inputs to local farmers.
scheme_details.important_dates: Executed in annual project phases. Details can be found at local Panchayat offices.

faqs.question: What is watershed development?
faqs.answer: It is the conservation and development of land, water, and vegetation resources in a specific geographical area (watershed) to restore ecological balance.

faqs.question: Is there any direct cash benefit to individual farmers?
faqs.answer: Rather than cash, farmers receive structural support like bunding on their land, construction of common check dams, free saplings, and training.

title: Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) India Organic Certification

scheme_details.tagline: Locally relevant, peer-reviewed, and low-cost organic certification for farmers.
scheme_details.department: National Centre of Organic and Natural Farming (NCONF), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.implemented_by: Regional Councils and Local Groups of Farmers
scheme_details.overview: Participatory Guarantee System (PGS) India is a decentralized organic certification system for agricultural products. It certifies organic products based on active participation of farmers, who act as peer inspectors to verify each other's organic practices.
eligibility: Individual farmers, organic farmer groups (minimum 5 members), and FPOs adopting organic cultivation methods.
Producers willing to follow PGS-India organic standards.
benefits: Extremely low-cost organic certification compared to third-party certifications.
Allows farmers to sell produce as certified 'PGS-Organic' and command premium prices.
Builds consumer trust through a transparent, online public database of certified farmers.
Promotes local group marketing and sharing of organic farming techniques.
documents_required: Signed pledge to adhere to organic cultivation standards
List of local group members and farm mapping sheet
application_process: Form a local group of at least 5 farmers from the same or nearby villages.
Register the group online on the PGS-India portal (pgsindia-ncof.gov.in) with aid from a Regional Council.
All members sign a pledge to avoid chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and GMO seeds.
Conduct mutual peer inspections during sowing, growth, and harvest phases, maintaining record books.
The group submits inspection summaries online to the Regional Council.
Once validated, the portal issues PGS-Organic certificates and labels for packaging.
scheme_details.important_dates: Ongoing registration. Peer inspections occur seasonally during active cropping cycles.

faqs.question: How is PGS different from third-party organic certification?
faqs.answer: PGS is peer-reviewed and group-managed, designed to be completely free/low-cost for small farmers, whereas third-party certification is commercial and requires auditing by external companies.

faqs.question: Can I export my crops with a PGS-Organic certificate?
faqs.answer: PGS-Organic is primary intended for domestic markets. For export, NPOP (National Programme for Organic Production) third-party certification is required.

scheme_details.tagline: Financial subsidy to purchase modern farm machinery and set up Custom Hiring Centres.
scheme_details.department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.overview: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM) aims to promote agricultural mechanization, particularly among small and marginal farmers, by providing subsidies for purchase of farm machinery (tractors, power tillers, rotavators) and establishing farm machinery banks.
eligibility: All categories of farmers, with special preference for small/marginal, women, SC, and ST farmers.
Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Cooperative Societies, and Rural Entrepreneurs.
scheme_details.land_limit: No fixed land holding limit specified

money_benefits.subsidy_rate: Subsidies ranging from 40% to 50% of the machinery cost. Higher subsidies up to 50% for SC, ST, and women farmers.
money_benefits.chc_grant: Financial assistance up to 40% for establishing Custom Hiring Centres (CHC) costing up to ₹10-25 lakh.

benefits: Makes modern machinery affordable to small-scale farmers.
Reduces labor dependence and saves time during sowing and harvesting.
Increases crop yield by ensuring timely land preparation.
Provides business opportunities to rural youth through rental centres.
documents_required: Caste Certificate (for higher SC/ST subsidy rates)
Quotation of the machinery to be purchased (from approved dealers)
application_process: Register on the direct benefit portal of your state (e.g., UP DBT, Bihar DBT, or the central agrimachinery.nic.in).
Apply online for the desired machinery subsidy and upload required documents (including dealer quotation).
The application is reviewed by block/district agriculture officers.
An approval/permit is issued to purchase the machinery from an authorized dealer.
After purchase, officers inspect the physical machine, verify the chassis/engine number, and credit the subsidy directly to your bank account.
scheme_details.important_dates: Subsidy targets are released annually at the beginning of the financial year (April-May).

faqs.question: Can I buy a tractor under this scheme?
faqs.answer: Yes, tractors, power tillers, laser land levelers, rotavators, and harvesters are all eligible for subsidies under SMAM.

faqs.question: What is a Custom Hiring Centre (CHC)?
faqs.answer: A CHC is a farm machinery bank from where small farmers can rent expensive equipment on an hourly basis, making mechanization accessible without buying the machines.

scheme_details.tagline: Soil and water conservation to enhance farming productivity in drylands.
scheme_details.department: Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development
scheme_details.implemented_by: State Nodal Agencies and District Watershed cells
scheme_details.overview: The Watershed Development Component of Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (WDC-PMKSY) focuses on soil and water conservation, groundwater recharge, runoff control, and restoring land productivity in rainfed and degraded agricultural areas.
eligibility: Farmers, self-help groups, and watershed community members living in notified watershed project regions.

money_benefits.development_fund: Grants to local watershed committees for constructing check dams, farm ponds, percolation tanks, and implementing soil health treatments.

benefits: Increases cropping intensity and irrigated area in drylands.
Prevents soil degradation and nutrient runoff.
Promotes organic fertilizers and water-saving irrigation methods.
Increases fodder availability for cattle, boosting dairy incomes.
documents_required: Land ownership records (showing the plot is in the project area)
application_process: The scheme is community-driven. State agencies select degraded/rainfed micro-watersheds.
A Watershed Committee is formed at the village level to map out works (e.g., digging ponds, constructing bunds).
Farmers request watershed treatments on their private lands during village meetings.
Approved civil works are executed by local labor, and materials/plants are provided to the farmers at zero or highly subsidized costs.
scheme_details.important_dates: Project cycles last between 3 to 5 years per selected watershed cluster.

faqs.question: How does this benefit a small farmer?
faqs.answer: It provides free/highly subsidized structural treatments on your farm (like contour bunds, trenches, or farm ponds) that preserve soil fertility and store water for dry seasons.

faqs.question: Who executes the watershed works?
faqs.answer: Works are executed locally, generating wage employment for agricultural laborers and rural communities under MGNREGA integration.

scheme_details.tagline: A unified national electronic market for transparent agricultural trade.
scheme_details.department: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
scheme_details.overview: National Agriculture Market (eNAM) is a pan-India electronic trading portal which networks the existing APMC mandis to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities. It ensures transparent bidding and direct payments to farmers.
eligibility: Individual farmers, Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), commission agents, traders, and agri-processors in states participating in eNAM.

money_benefits.direct_payment: Proceeds from electronic bids are transferred directly into the farmer's verified bank account within 24 hours.
money_benefits.free_registration: No registration fees or hidden agent commissions for online trade.

benefits: Price discovery: Farmers get bids from traders across the country, ensuring the highest price for their crop.
Eliminates local cartels and middleman exploitation.
Quality assaying: Scientific testing of crop parameters before bidding ensures price reflects quality.
Instant online payments directly to bank accounts.
documents_required: Bank Account Details (Passbook copy / Cancelled Cheque)
Land records (for farmer verification in some mandis)
application_process: Go to the eNAM portal (enam.gov.in) or download the eNAM Mobile App.
Click on 'Registration' and select 'User Type' as 'Farmer' or 'FPO'.
Fill out name, bank account details, and address.
Upload a copy of your bank passbook/cancelled cheque and submit.
Alternatively, visit the eNAM helpdesk at your local APMC mandi. Mandi staff will register you instantly.
Bring your produce to the mandi, get it sampled/tested (assayed), and traders will bid on the eNAM portal. The highest bid is shown to you; on approval, the sale is completed.
scheme_details.important_dates: Ongoing service. Open daily for commodity trading during mandi operating hours.

faqs.question: Is registration on eNAM free?
faqs.answer: Yes, registration for farmers on the eNAM portal and mobile app is completely free.

faqs.question: How do I get paid for my crop sales?
faqs.answer: Once you accept the highest bid on eNAM, the trader transfers the amount electronically, which is deposited directly into your registered bank account.

faqs.question: Can I trade from my home?
faqs.answer: Farmers can check prices and manage listings from home using the app. However, crops must be brought to the integrated mandi for quality testing and weighing to finalize the trade.
